title: Man dead, officer injured after shooting in Winnipeg parking lot
article: A man was shot to death and a Winnipeg police officer injured, possibly by his own gun, during a scuffle in a gas station parking lot, a police spokesman said.

Patrol Sgt. Gordon Hudson said officer Jason Michalyshen, who has less than two years experience, was wounded by a bullet in the upper leg on Monday night. A bullet also killed Donald Miles, 34, who was wanted on a Canada-wide warrant for parole violation.
The Winnipeg resident had been serving two years for several convictions including assaulting a police officer when he was recently granted statutory release.
Hudson couldn't say how many shots were fired, or if the officer shot himself or was hit by a ricochet.
Hudson said the trouble started when two officers driving by on routine patrol spotted a man brandishing a knife. Two more officers joined the scene moments later.
The officers demanded Miles drop his knife and used more than one can of pepper spray to try to subdue him, Hudson said.
He was shot after he lunged at the officers, Hudson said.

Earlier reports had suggested the officer was hurt while trying to break up a fight, but Hudson said that as far as he knew, the only people involved were the man with the knife and the four officers.
An autopsy was being conducted on the suspect.

Homicide detectives were investigating the shooting and seized the service revolvers of all the officers involved, Hudson said. The four were placed on temporary leave while the investigation continues.
Mark Michalyshen, Jason's brother, said he was released from hospital Tuesday.
"He got hit in his left thigh the bullet entered and exited," said Mark.
"He's doing OK. He's a little shook up mentally, but physically he's OK."
